source.title: Long-term memory prepares neural activity for perception
source.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

confidence_rationale: Multi-method (behaviour + EEG + fMRI) evidence that LTM content modulates anticipatory state in visual cortex in a spatially specific way before the stimulus arrives, i.e. a top-down change in sensory-level sampling readiness without sensory relearning. Hippocampal involvement is inferred from network fMRI, not isolated or manipulated, and distortion is untested.
failure_signatures: The hippocampus is implicated only as part of an 'integrated cortical network' in fMRI; the paper does not show that hippocampal signals are the proximal cause of the preparatory modulation in extrastriate cortex.
Predictions derived from memory were valid on the tested trials; the design cannot show whether a mis-learned location would bias preparatory activity equivalently.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Contents of long-term memory sharpen perceptual sensitivity at memory-predicted locations; memory-guided attention is associated with spatially specific alpha-band desynchronization over visual cortex and spatiotopic modulation of preparatory activity in extrastriate cortex; a network including the hippocampus and dorsal frontoparietal cortex is a likely organiser of these preparatory states.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports the MECH-082 notion that map-derived predictions reconfigure sensory-level (E1) sampling readiness in advance of input, per spatial dimension, with the sensory encoder's weights untouched. The spatiotopic alpha modulation is a candidate biological readout for the 'per-dimension E1 sampling allocation' DV the claim's what_would_answer calls for.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Alpha desynchronization and BOLD preparatory activity index gain/readiness, not learning-free 'sampling allocation' in REE's exact sense. The hippocampal link is network-level and correlational. No map distortion, no E2 intermediary, and no feedback-channel ablation, so the claim's discriminating contrast (bias present with feedback intact, absent when cut) is not addressed.
mapping.source_context: Healthy human adults; memory-guided spatial attention paradigm; behavioural sensitivity, EEG oscillations, and fMRI across experiments.

confidence_components.notes: PNAS, convergent methods. Best available precedent for a per-dimension sampling DV, but hippocampal causality is not isolated.
